newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says no reports on Red Army in Colombia.
newsitem.headline: Japan says no reports on Red Army in Colombia.

text.p: Japanese government officials said on Friday they could not confirm reports that members of the elusive Japan Red Army were in Colombia's northwest region.
"We have no conclusive information about the whereabouts of Japan Red Army members," an official at the Foreign Ministry's Terrorism Prevention Division said.
The ministry division is in charge of monitoring the movements of the Lebanon-based Japan Red Army.

Sources in Colombia's national security department DAS said on Thursday that Japan Red Army guerrillas, including leader Fusako Shigenobu, 51, may be training Colombian guerrillas in the troubled Uraba region in the northwest.
In February, five Red Army members were arrested in Beirut and have been charged with using false passports. Japan has sought the extradition of the five but Lebanon decided to put them on trial.
The Japan Red Army was formed by Shigenobu in 1969, and since the early 1970s has been based in Lebanon.
